name: OOP & Design Patterns
description: Object-oriented design, SOLID principles, the classic design patterns and low-level design practice.

nodes.name: OOP basics
nodes.desc: Objects, classes, state and behaviour and why we model with objects.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model a problem as objects that combine state and behaviour and explain why object-oriented design helps.

nodes.name: Encapsulation
nodes.desc: Hiding state behind an interface and enforcing invariants.
nodes.summary: You will be able to hide an object's internal state behind a public interface and enforce invariants that keep it valid.

nodes.name: Polymorphism
nodes.desc: Subtyping, overriding and dynamic dispatch.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use subtyping, method overriding and dynamic dispatch to write code that works with many object types.

nodes.name: Composition
nodes.desc: Favouring composition over inheritance and delegation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose composition over inheritance and build behaviour by delegating to collaborating objects.

nodes.name: SOLID principles
nodes.desc: Single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov, interface segregation and dependency inversion.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the five SOLID principles to judge and improve the structure of object-oriented code.

nodes.name: UML class diagrams
nodes.desc: Class and sequence diagrams for communicating a design.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read and draw UML class and sequence diagrams to communicate a design clearly.

nodes.name: Coupling & cohesion
nodes.desc: Measuring how well modules are separated and focused.
nodes.summary: You will be able to assess how tightly modules depend on each other and how focused each one is, and improve both.

nodes.name: Dependency injection
nodes.desc: Injecting collaborators, inversion of control and testable code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to supply collaborators from outside a class using dependency injection to make code flexible and testable.

nodes.name: Factory & builder
nodes.desc: Factory method, abstract factory and builder.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decouple object creation from use with factory method, abstract factory and builder patterns.

nodes.name: Singleton
nodes.desc: Singleton, its problems, and alternatives through dependency injection.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement a singleton, explain the problems global state causes and replace it with dependency injection.

nodes.name: Adapter & facade
nodes.desc: Adapting interfaces and simplifying subsystems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to adapt incompatible interfaces with the adapter pattern and simplify complex subsystems with a facade.

nodes.name: Decorator & proxy
nodes.desc: Wrapping objects to add behaviour or control access.
nodes.summary: You will be able to add behaviour by wrapping objects with decorators and control access to them with proxies.

nodes.name: Composite
nodes.desc: Treating trees of objects uniformly.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent part-whole hierarchies with the composite pattern so clients treat leaves and groups uniformly.
topics: Examples like file systems and UI trees

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.desc: Swapping algorithms behind a common interface.
nodes.summary: You will be able to swap interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface using the strategy pattern.

nodes.name: Observer
nodes.desc: Publish/subscribe between objects and event systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to let objects subscribe to and react to changes in another object using the observer pattern.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.desc: Requests as objects for undo, queues and macros.
nodes.summary: You will be able to encapsulate requests as command objects to support undo, queuing and macros.

nodes.name: State & template
nodes.desc: State machines as objects and algorithms with overridable steps.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model state-dependent behaviour with the state pattern and define algorithm skeletons with the template method.

nodes.name: Iterator & visitor
nodes.desc: Traversing structures and adding operations without changing classes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to traverse collections with iterators and add new operations to object structures using the visitor pattern.

nodes.name: Refactor to patterns
nodes.desc: Recognising code smells and refactoring safely toward patterns.
nodes.summary: You will be able to spot code smells and refactor code safely toward appropriate design patterns under test protection.

nodes.name: Anti-patterns
nodes.desc: God objects, overengineering and pattern misuse.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise design anti-patterns such as god objects and overengineering and know how to avoid them.

nodes.name: Parking lot LLD
nodes.desc: Design and implement a parking lot system with clean classes and tests.
nodes.summary: You will design and implement a parking lot system with clear classes, responsibilities and unit tests as a low-level design exercise.

nodes.name: Text editor project
nodes.desc: Build a small text editor with undo/redo, plugins and change notifications.
nodes.summary: You will build a small text editor that supports undo and redo, plugins and change notifications using several design patterns.
